site.appDescription: Free, open-source VS Code extension that turns everything Claude Code keeps on your machine — sessions, usage and quota, accounts, MCP servers, skills, commands, hooks, agents, plugins, checkpoints, prompts and memory — into one searchable sidebar. 100% local, no telemetry.
site.llmsIntro: Claude Code Manager reads the files Claude Code keeps in ~/.claude/, ~/.claude.json and a project's .claude/ folder, and shows them as 12 sidebar tabs in VS Code and VS Code-based editors (Cursor, Devin Desktop/Windsurf, Kiro, VSCodium and others that install from Open VSX). It works with the Claude Code CLI and with Anthropic's official Claude Code extension: sessions from both appear in one list. It has no network client and collects no telemetry. The opt-in Quota card reads Claude Code's own statusline data from a local cache file; it never calls Anthropic. Account profiles keep a local, plaintext copy of each saved login's tokens in ~/.claude/manager-accounts/. It is an independent project, not made by Anthropic.

pages.title: Claude Code Manager — A VS Code Sidebar for Claude Code
pages.description: Free VS Code extension for Claude Code: search and resume sessions, track usage and limits, switch accounts, and manage MCP, skills, hooks and agents.
pages.h1: Claude Code Manager

og.title: Everything Claude Code keeps on your machine, in one VS Code sidebar
og.alt: Claude Code Manager: everything Claude Code keeps on your machine, in one VS Code sidebar

faq.q: Is Claude Code Manager made by Anthropic?
faq.a: No. It is an independent, open-source extension (Apache-2.0) built by Vishal Gupta. It reads the files Claude Code keeps on your machine and works alongside Anthropic's own Claude Code extension.

faq.q: Does it send anything over the network?
faq.a: No. The extension has no network client and no telemetry. It reads and writes local files, and it starts the claude CLI in a terminal only when you ask it to (for example to log in or install a plugin) — the CLI does its own networking.

faq.q: Do I need Claude Code installed?
faq.a: Yes. Install Claude Code first — the CLI, the official VS Code extension, or both. Claude Code Manager reads the same ~/.claude/ folder, so sessions from either show up in one list.

faq.q: Which editors does it work in?
faq.a: VS Code 1.90 or later, and VS Code-based editors. Cursor, Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf), Kiro and VSCodium install it from Open VSX; see editors.

faq.q: Does it touch my Claude Code tokens?
faq.a: Only if you save account profiles. The Quota card never uses your token. Saving a profile for account switching keeps a local, plaintext copy of that login's tokens in ~/.claude/manager-accounts/, and the extension tells you so the first time. Nothing leaves your machine.

faq.q: Is it free?
faq.a: Yes. Free and open source under Apache-2.0, with no account or sign-up. Sponsorship is optional.

pages.h1: The Claude Code session manager for VS Code
pages.lede: Every conversation Claude Code has had on your machine, in one list. Search what was said, see which project and git branch it ran on, and resume it in a terminal or in the official extension's chat.

shot.alt: Sessions tab listing Claude Code sessions grouped by date, with project and branch filters and live status dots

og.title: Search and resume every Claude Code session

faq.q: How do I find an old Claude Code session?
faq.a: Open the Sessions tab, set the date filter to All, and type something you remember from the conversation — the search reads the full transcripts, not just titles. Filter by project or git branch to narrow it down, then click Resume.

faq.q: Does it show sessions from the official Claude Code extension?
faq.a: Yes. The CLI and the official extension write to the same ~/.claude/projects/ folder, so sessions from both appear in one list. With sessions.resumeIn set to auto (the default), Resume opens a session where it started.

faq.q: Does deleting a session delete the transcript?
faq.a: No. Delete hides the session from the list and leaves Claude Code's files untouched. The one exception is a temporary session you start on purpose: its transcript is removed when its terminal closes.

faq.q: Can I move a session to another machine?
faq.a: Yes. Export it as a .jsonl file (or several as a .zip), copy it over, and use Import on the other machine. The import places it in the right project folder so claude --resume finds it.

faq.q: What happens if I resume on the wrong git branch?
faq.a: You get a warning first. If the session ran on a different branch, the extension offers to check it out, to open the worktree where that branch is already checked out, or to resume anyway.

pages.llms: token usage by model, project, tool and MCP server over 7 days, 30 days and all time, an activity heatmap, and an opt-in Quota card plus status-bar item showing the 5-hour and 7-day limit percentages from Claude Code's own statusline data (cached locally). Cost is an estimate at public API rates.
pages.h1: Track Claude Code usage and your limits
pages.lede: How many tokens went where — by model, by project, by tool — and how much of your 5-hour and weekly allowance is left, right in the VS Code status bar. Worked out from files already on your disk.

shot.alt: Usage view with token totals, per-model breakdown and an activity heatmap

og.title: Claude Code usage and 5-hour / weekly limits, locally

faq.q: How do I see my Claude Code usage in VS Code?
faq.a: Open the Account tab. Usage shows tokens, sessions and cache reads for the last 7 days, 30 days or all time, broken down by model, project, tool and MCP server. Turn on the Quota card to see your 5-hour and weekly limits too.

faq.q: Where do the 5-hour and weekly numbers come from?
faq.a: From Claude Code itself. Claude Code passes rate_limits to its statusline command; the opt-in tap saves that to a local file, and the extension reads the file. It never calls Anthropic and never uses your token. The figures are as fresh as Claude Code's last update, and the card says when that was.

faq.q: Why doesn't the Quota card show anything yet?
faq.a: It needs two things: the statusline tap switched on, and at least one Claude Code reply after that. Claude Code only includes limit data for Pro and Max subscribers (or behind a gateway with a spend limit), after the first response in a session.

faq.q: Is the cost figure my bill?
faq.a: No. It is what those tokens would cost at public API rates, from a price table in the extension. Pro and Max subscriptions are billed at a flat price.

faq.q: What changes on my machine when I turn the Quota card on?
faq.a: One entry: statusLine.command in ~/.claude/settings.json, pointing at the tap. Your existing statusline still runs — the tap passes the data on to it. Turning the card off removes the entry.

pages.title: Switch Claude Code Accounts Without /logout — VS Code
pages.description: Save each Claude login as a profile and switch between work and personal accounts in two clicks, without the /logout and /login cycle. Free and local.
pages.summary: Save logins as profiles and switch without /logout and /login.
pages.llms: save the signed-in Claude account as a profile and switch between profiles without /logout and /login; swaps only the login identity and credentials (macOS Keychain or ~/.claude/.credentials.json); profiles keep a local plaintext copy of tokens in ~/.claude/manager-accounts/.
pages.h1: Switch Claude accounts without logging out
pages.lede: Save each Claude login once — work, personal, a team seat — and switch between them from the sidebar or the command palette. No browser round-trip each time.

shot.alt: Account tab with the profile switcher, quota bars and usage summary

og.title: Switch Claude Code accounts without /logout

faq.q: How do I switch accounts in Claude Code?
faq.a: Without an extension, run /logout then /login and sign in again in the browser. With Claude Code Manager, save each account as a profile once, then pick it from the Account tab or run Claude Code Manager: Switch Account from the command palette.

faq.q: Where are saved profiles stored, and is that safe?
faq.a: In ~/.claude/manager-accounts/<profile>/, on your machine only. Each profile holds a copy of that login's tokens in plaintext — the same format Claude Code uses in ~/.claude/.credentials.json on Linux and Windows — so treat the folder as sensitive. Deleting a profile deletes its copy immediately.

faq.q: What exactly changes when I switch?
faq.a: Only the login: the account identity in ~/.claude.json and the Claude credential entry (the macOS Keychain or .credentials.json). Your projects, MCP servers and settings stay as they are.

faq.q: Is there an official way to use two accounts?
faq.a: Yes: Anthropic's docs suggest giving each account its own configuration directory with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. That keeps separate settings and history per account. Profiles are for switching one setup between logins.

pages.lede: MCP servers can come from a project's .mcp.json, any parent folder, your user config or a plugin. See them all in one list, switch them on and off, and add new ones from a form.

shot.alt: MCP Servers tab listing servers by source with enable switches and masked secrets

og.title: Every Claude Code MCP server, one switch each

faq.q: How do I disable an MCP server in Claude Code?
faq.a: In Claude Code, toggle it off in the /mcp panel. In Claude Code Manager, flip its switch in the MCP tab. Either way the configuration is kept. The step-by-step guide covers every option.

faq.q: Why don't I see a server in Claude Code?
faq.a: It may come from a file you're not looking at — a .mcp.json in a parent folder, your user config, or a plugin. The MCP tab lists each server with its source, and a banner flags servers that need you to sign in again.

faq.q: Are my API keys shown?
faq.a: No. Values that look like secrets are masked in the list.

faq.q: Can I add a server without writing JSON?
faq.a: Yes. Use the form, or pick one of the 16 servers in the bundled catalog (it ships with the extension; nothing is downloaded).

og.title: Every Claude Code skill, every scope, one list

faq.q: Where does Claude Code look for skills?
faq.a: In ~/.claude/skills/ (yours, for every project), .claude/skills/ in the project, and inside installed plugins. Each skill is a folder with a SKILL.md.

faq.q: What's the difference between skills and slash commands?
faq.a: Claude Code's docs say custom commands have been merged into skills: .claude/commands/deploy.md and .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md both create /deploy. Skills can bundle extra files. Both still work.

faq.q: Can I create a skill from the sidebar?
faq.a: Not yet. You can open, launch and delete skills; create one by adding a folder with a SKILL.md.

pages.lede: Claude Code ships with {{commandsCount}} built-in slash commands, and you can add your own. Here is the full built-in list with what each one does — the same list the Commands tab shows, next to your custom and plugin commands.

shot.alt: Commands tab listing built-in and custom slash commands with descriptions

og.title: Every Claude Code slash command, with what it does

faq.q: How do I see all Claude Code commands?
faq.a: Type / in Claude Code to get suggestions, or see the full list on this page. The Commands tab in Claude Code Manager shows the built-ins next to your own and your plugins' commands.

faq.q: How do I make a custom slash command?
faq.a: Add a Markdown file to .claude/commands/ (for one project) or ~/.claude/commands/ (for all projects): review.md becomes /review. Claude Code's docs now treat these as skills, and .claude/skills/review/SKILL.md works the same way.

faq.q: Why doesn't my custom command show up?
faq.a: Check the file is in a commands folder Claude Code reads (project or home), ends in .md, and that no skill has the same name — on a clash, the skill wins.

shot.alt: Hooks tab listing hooks by event and scope with their commands

og.title: Every Claude Code hook, with an off switch

faq.q: Where are Claude Code hooks configured?
faq.a: Under hooks in a settings file: ~/.claude/settings.json (all projects), .claude/settings.json (the project, shared) or .claude/settings.local.json (the project, just you).

faq.q: How do I turn off a hook without deleting it?
faq.a: Flip its switch in the Hooks tab. The hook moves to a _disabled_hooks entry in the same file, so turning it back on restores it exactly.

faq.q: Which hook events are there?
faq.a: The table on this page lists all {{hookEventsCount}} events the editor offers, from SessionStart to SessionEnd, with when each one fires.

faq.q: Where are Claude Code subagents stored?
faq.a: In ~/.claude/agents/ (yours, for every project) and .claude/agents/ (the project). Plugins can ship agents too.

faq.q: How do I set a subagent's model?
faq.a: With the model field in its frontmatter — for example sonnet, opus, haiku, a full model ID, or inherit. The Agents tab shows the model on each row.

og.title: Claude Code plugins: what's installed and what's on

faq.q: Where does Claude Code install plugins?
faq.a: In ~/.claude/plugins/. Which plugins are switched on is stored separately, under enabledPlugins in your settings files.

faq.q: How does it install a plugin?
faq.a: It runs Claude Code's own command, claude plugin install <plugin> --scope <scope>, in a terminal, so Claude Code does the install exactly as it would by hand.

pages.title: Claude Code Checkpoints: Diff and Restore Edited Files
pages.description: Claude Code backs up files before it edits them. Diff any backed-up version against your file and restore it, from a VS Code sidebar.
pages.summary: Diff and restore any version of a file Claude Code edited.
pages.llms: lists the file versions Claude Code saved in ~/.claude/file-history/ per session; diff any version against the file on disk and restore it (with a confirmation).
pages.h1: See every file Claude edited, and put it back
pages.lede: Before Claude Code edits a file it keeps a copy in ~/.claude/file-history/. The Checkpoints tab lists those versions per session, opens a diff against what's on disk now, and restores the one you want.

og.title: Diff and restore files Claude Code edited

faq.q: How is this different from /rewind?
faq.a: /rewind (or Esc twice) rolls back inside a session, conversation and code together. The Checkpoints tab works from the saved file versions on disk, so you can diff or restore a single file at any time, even after the session ended.

faq.q: Does it cover changes made by shell commands?
faq.a: No. Claude Code's checkpoints don't track files changed by Bash commands (like rm or mv) or by editing outside Claude Code, so there's no copy to restore.

og.title: Search every prompt you've typed into Claude Code

faq.q: Where does Claude Code save my prompts?
faq.a: In ~/.claude/history.jsonl, one line per prompt, with the project it was typed in.

faq.q: Can I open the conversation a prompt came from?
faq.a: Yes. Each prompt links back to its session, which opens in the Sessions tab.

og.title: Read and prune Claude Code's auto memory

faq.q: Where is Claude Code's auto memory stored?
faq.a: In ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/, with MEMORY.md as the index. It's separate from CLAUDE.md, which you write yourself.

faq.q: What are broken links and orphans?
faq.a: A broken link is an index entry pointing at a file that no longer exists. An orphan is a memory file the index doesn't mention, so it may never be loaded.

faq.q: Where is Claude Code's settings.json?
faq.a: Yours is ~/.claude/settings.json. A project can add .claude/settings.json (shared) and .claude/settings.local.json (just you). See the map of Claude Code's files.

faq.q: Can I undo a settings change?
faq.a: Yes. A snapshot is taken before every write the extension makes; restore any of them from the Config tab.

faq.q: Can I copy my setup to another machine?
faq.a: Yes. Export Brain zips your CLAUDE.md, settings, skills, commands, agents, memory and user-level MCP servers; Import Brain previews conflicts before writing them on the other machine.

pages.title: Where Claude Code Stores Session History (and Recovery)
pages.description: Claude Code saves sessions as JSONL in ~/.claude/projects/. Where to find them, why old ones disappear after 30 days, and how to resume or move one.
pages.summary: Where transcripts live, why they disappear, how to get one back.

pages.h1: Where Claude Code stores your sessions
pages.lede: Every Claude Code conversation is a file on your disk. Here is where it lives, how long Claude Code keeps it, and how to get back to an old one.

og.title: Where Claude Code stores your sessions, and how to find them

faq.q: Why did my old Claude Code sessions disappear?
faq.a: Most likely the cleanup sweep. Claude Code deletes transcripts older than cleanupPeriodDays — 30 days by default — without a message. Raise it in ~/.claude/settings.json (it can't be 0) to keep them longer.

faq.q: Can I read the JSONL files directly?
faq.a: You can, but Anthropic's docs warn the format is internal and changes between versions. Use /export, or a tool that reads them for you.

pages.lede: Pro and Max plans have two limits that matter in Claude Code: a five-hour session limit and a weekly limit. This guide sticks to what Anthropic documents, and shows where to see your own numbers.

og.title: Claude Code's 5-hour and weekly limits, explained

faq.q: Are Claude and Claude Code limits shared?
faq.a: Yes. Anthropic's help center says the limits are shared across Claude and Claude Code, so chatting on claude.ai uses the same allowance.

faq.q: How do I check how much I have left?
faq.a: In Claude Code, run /usage (plan usage limits and activity) or /status. In VS Code, Claude Code Manager's Quota card and status bar show both windows as percentages.

faq.q: What's the difference between ~/.claude.json and ~/.claude/settings.json?
faq.a: ~/.claude/settings.json is your settings file (permissions, hooks, model, statusline). ~/.claude.json holds app state: your login identity, MCP servers at user and local scope, and per-project state.

faq.q: Can I change where Claude Code keeps its files?
faq.a: Yes: set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to another folder before starting claude. Claude Code Manager reads the same variable.

pages.h1: How to disable an MCP server in Claude Code
pages.lede: Too many MCP servers slow Claude Code down and crowd its context with tools. You can switch one off and keep its configuration, or remove it entirely. Here is each option and what it changes.

og.title: How to disable an MCP server in Claude Code

faq.q: Does disabling a server delete its configuration?
faq.a: No. Toggling a server off in /mcp keeps it listed as disabled; turn it back on any time. claude mcp remove is the command that deletes it.

faq.q: Is disabledMcpjsonServers the same as disabling?
faq.a: No. Anthropic's docs say enabledMcpjsonServers and disabledMcpjsonServers control approval of servers from a project's .mcp.json, and are unrelated to the on/off toggle.

pages.lede: Claude Code Manager overlaps with several good tools. These pages compare facts from each project's own documentation, and say plainly where the other tool is the better pick.

pages.title: Claude Code Manager vs the Official Claude Code Extension
pages.description: What Anthropic's Claude Code extension does, what Claude Code Manager adds, and why most people run both. A fact-based comparison with links to the docs.
pages.summary: Different jobs: the chat client vs a manager for what it leaves on disk.
pages.llms: Anthropic's official Claude Code extension is the chat client (with session history, /usage and a Customize panel); Claude Code Manager is a sidebar for the files Claude Code keeps on disk, adding account profiles, checkpoint diff/restore, prompt-history search, memory browsing, settings snapshots and usage breakdowns. They are designed to run together.
pages.h1: Claude Code Manager and the official extension
pages.lede: They do different jobs. Anthropic's extension is where you talk to Claude. Claude Code Manager is a sidebar for everything Claude Code leaves on your disk. Most people who install one keep both.

og.title: Claude Code Manager and the official extension: use both

pages.title: ccusage Alternative for VS Code — Claude Code Manager
pages.description: ccusage reports Claude Code usage in the terminal. Claude Code Manager shows usage and your 5-hour and weekly limits in VS Code. Facts and trade-offs.
pages.summary: CLI reports vs an in-editor view with live limits.
pages.llms: ccusage is a widely used CLI for Claude Code usage and cost reports (daily, monthly, per session); Claude Code Manager shows usage breakdowns and the 5-hour/weekly limit percentages inside VS Code. ccusage is better for scripted and terminal reports.
pages.h1: ccusage or Claude Code Manager?
pages.lede: Both read the usage data Claude Code leaves on your machine. ccusage turns it into reports in your terminal; Claude Code Manager shows it in your editor next to your limits. Here's how to pick.

og.title: ccusage or Claude Code Manager?

pages.title: claude-swap Alternative: Switch Claude Accounts in VS Code
pages.description: claude-swap switches Claude Code accounts from the CLI and can rotate on rate limits. Claude Code Manager switches them from VS Code. Facts and trade-offs.
pages.summary: A CLI switcher with auto-rotation vs one-click switching in the editor.
pages.llms: claude-swap is a Python CLI for switching Claude Code accounts, including automatic rotation on rate limits; Claude Code Manager switches saved profiles from VS Code alongside usage and quota. claude-swap is better for terminal-only and automated rotation.
pages.h1: claude-swap or Claude Code Manager?
pages.lede: Both save more than one Claude login and switch between them without the browser. claude-swap does it from the terminal; Claude Code Manager does it from your editor's sidebar.

og.title: claude-swap or Claude Code Manager?
